name: International Rescue Committee: crisis response, recovery and development (charityevals' estimate)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: the IRC's CRRD spending by region in its statement of functional expenses for the year to September 2025 (Africa $362.5m, the Middle East and Ukraine $142.3m, Asia $101.9m, Latin America $29.2m; emergency preparedness and technical units spread the same way), each region split equally over its main programme countries on the 2025 Annual Report's map (a judgment: no country split is published).
summary: The International Rescue Committee's work in crisis-affected countries (Crisis Response, Recovery and Development: $754m of its $1.14bn programme spending in the year to September 2025), split by sector from its own outcome split: health care at 2,713 supported facilities, contraception, nutrition treatment for 638,187 children and 85,163 mothers, about 8 million vaccine doses, water for 2.5 million people, $52.5m in cash to 1.5 million people, livelihoods, women's and children's protection, and learning for 602,546 children. It comes to about {{result}} years of healthy life per $1,000 (combined range 0.11-1.3), because much of its money goes to treating malnutrition and cash, whose reach it counts: nutrition gives about two fifths, other health care and cash about a sixth each, contraception and vaccination about a fifteenth each. The biggest uncertainties are the deaths averted per child treated and what health care costs per person covered; every branch but cash is discounted for missing data (no controlled measure of the IRC's own effect).

sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

source.page: printed p. 5 (PDF p. 6), consolidated statement of functional expenses (amounts in thousands)

rows.explainer: Salaries and benefits of the IRC's own staff across programmes and support (statement of functional expenses), for the donor section's staff share.

rows.label: Share of CRRD spending on health (primary and reproductive care, nutrition, vaccination, water)
rows.explainer: Judgment 60% (52-66%): health is 43% of all the IRC's programme services (both lines) in its own split by Strategy100 outcome (2025 Annual Report, Executive Summary p. 6: Health 43%, Safety 24%, Economic Well-being 22%, Education 10%, Power 1%; the accounts don't split CRRD by sector), almost all of it abroad; the resettlement line (34% of programme spending) is mostly case management, employment, legal and reception services, with some refugee health and mental health care. If resettlement's health share is 5-20%, CRRD's is (43% - 34% × 5-20%) / 66% = 55-63%.

rows.label: Share of CRRD spending on safety (protection, women's protection, child protection), with Power
rows.explainer: Judgment 17% (11-23%): safety is 24% of all programme services and Power 1% ; much of resettlement's work counts as safety (immigration legal services, children's legal services, anti-trafficking, humanitarian reception), so CRRD's share is lower. Power (client feedback and governance work, 1%) is folded in here: it serves the same clients.

rows.label: Share of CRRD spending on education
rows.explainer: Judgment 8% (5-11%): education is 10% of all programme services ; resettlement's English classes and youth programmes take some of it.

rows.label: Share of CRRD spending on economic well-being (cash, livelihoods)
rows.explainer: The rest: about {{row:crrd_share_econ}}, against 22% of all programme services , resettlement's employment and financial services taking the difference.

rows.label: CRRD health spending (US$)
rows.explainer: CRRD expenses × the health share; split below into nutrition, vaccination, water and other care.

rows.label: CRRD safety spending (US$)
rows.explainer: CRRD expenses × the safety share.

rows.label: CRRD education spending (US$)
rows.explainer: CRRD expenses × the education share.

rows.label: CRRD economic well-being spending (US$)
rows.explainer: CRRD expenses × the economic well-being share: cash assistance and livelihoods.

rows.label: Spending on the modelled programme, year to September 2025 (US$)
rows.explainer: All of CRRD ($754.0m), split into its sectors. It includes the nutrition and vaccination work GiveWell funds, which GiveWell's own IRC models cover too; this model covers every sector of the line itself.

rows.label: Overhead ratio
rows.explainer: Total expenses ÷ programme expenses: management and fundraising spread over both programme lines by cost.

rows.label: Total cost of the modelled programme (US$)
rows.explainer: CRRD spending with its share of overhead.

rows.label: Other health care: cost per person covered by IRC-supported facilities for a year (US$)
rows.explainer: Judgment $25 (12-50) a person a year: the IRC supported 2,713 static and mobile health facilities; costed basic packages of primary care in low-income and humanitarian settings run at about $10-40 a person covered a year (Afghanistan's basic package, about $10 a head, at the low end; mobile clinics in insecure areas and reproductive and mental health care at the high end). No count of people covered or consultations is published for 2025.

rows.label: Other health care spending: primary, maternal and mental health care (US$)
rows.explainer: Health spending less family planning, nutrition, vaccination and water, each costed below.

rows.label: Other health care: people covered by IRC-supported care for a year
rows.explainer: Other health spending ÷ the cost per person covered: about 12 million people. As a check, the branches' reach (other care 12m, water 2.5m, cash 1.5m, nutrition 0.7m, education 0.6m, vaccination 0.8m) sums to about 18 million before overlap, against the 20.5 million the IRC and its partners reached directly in crisis countries.

rows.label: Other health care: cost per person covered, with overhead (US$)
rows.explainer: For reading: the branch's cost per person with its share of overhead.

rows.label: Share of the people covered who live in acute crises
rows.explainer: Judgment 35% (20-50%): the acute emergencies of 2025 (Sudan, eastern DRC, Gaza, South Sudan's border areas, Somalia's drought) against the protracted crises and displacement settings that make up most of the IRC's 40 countries (Nigeria, Afghanistan, Kenya's camps, Syria, Yemen, Ethiopia, Latin America, Ukraine). Africa is 57% of CRRD spending by region (statement of functional expenses), most of it in protracted settings.

rows.label: Death rate in acute crises, as a multiple of the normal rate
rows.explainer: Judgment 3× (2-5×): Sphere calls a doubling of the baseline crude death rate an emergency; mortality surveys in camps and besieged areas commonly find 0.5-1 deaths per 10,000 a day against a baseline of about 0.2-0.25, 2-4.5 times.

rows.label: Death rate in protracted crises, as a multiple of the normal rate
rows.explainer: Judgment 1.3× (1.1-1.6×): protracted displacement settings run close to, but above, their country's normal rate; surveys there mostly find crude death rates below Sphere's emergency threshold.

rows.label: Death rate among the people covered, during the crisis, without the response
rows.explainer: The normal rate × the mix of acute and protracted settings: about 0.016 a person-year, inside the 0.011-0.037 a year that mortality surveys in African and Middle Eastern crises commonly find (0.3-1 per 10,000 a day), towards the low end because much of the work is in protracted settings.

rows.label: Normal death rate of the populations served
rows.explainer: UN WPP crude death rates for 2024 in three of the IRC's largest crisis countries (shared facts): the population's rate outside the crisis.

rows.label: Share of the excess deaths among those covered that the care averts
rows.explainer: Judgment 10% (3-25%): most excess deaths in crises are from malaria, diarrhoea, pneumonia, measles and complications of birth, which primary care treats; integrated community case management and facility care cut child deaths by a quarter or more where fully delivered (Lassi & Bhutta 2015, Cochrane, community packages RR 0.75 for neonatal deaths), but coverage of a catchment is partial and part of the excess comes from violence, hunger and lost shelter. Malnutrition treatment, vaccination and water are counted in their own branches, not here.

rows.label: Years of the crisis the care covers
rows.explainer: Judgment a year (9 months to a year): the reach is a year's flow of people covered against a year's spending; some facilities are supported for only part of the year.

rows.label: Other health care: deaths averted per person covered
rows.explainer: Excess mortality × the share averted × the time covered.

rows.label: Share of the deaths averted that are of children under five
rows.explainer: A stand-in: the site's WHO-based split of diarrhoeal deaths in sub-Saharan Africa (facts/death_ages.json), for excess crisis deaths, which are mostly infections worsened by hunger and displacement: 55% under five. No all-cause split for the crisis countries is in the site's facts.

rows.label: Share of deaths over five that are of children 5-14
rows.explainer: From the same stand-in split.

rows.label: Share of adult deaths that are at 15-49
rows.explainer: From the same stand-in split; the rest valued at the 50-74 band.

rows.label: Value of a death averted, by the age mix (units of value)
rows.explainer: The shared value of a death by age band, mixed by the shares above, × the life-value slider.

rows.label: Value of averting a child's death (units of value)
rows.explainer: The shared value of a death under five × the life-value slider, for nutrition, vaccination and water.

rows.label: Other health care: illness averted per person covered (healthy years)
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.003 (0.001-0.008) healthy years a person-year: illness treated (malaria, infections, complications of birth, depression), against a crisis population's disability burden of about 0.1 healthy years a person-year; the share averted is the same order as the deaths'.

rows.label: Other health care: value of goods handed out per person, beyond care (US$)
rows.explainer: Zero by construction: care is valued as the deaths and illness it averts. Cash and the goods of the economic programmes are in their own branches.

rows.label: Price level: international dollars per US dollar (2017 PPP)
rows.explainer: The shared PPP factors of four of the IRC's large African programmes, for the cash branch.

rows.label: Consumption per person per year of the people reached (2017 PPP $)
rows.explainer: Judgment $700 PPP a year ($400-1,200): displaced and crisis-hit households in low-income countries, around the extreme-poverty line ($2.15 a day, $785 a year).

rows.label: Other health care: gain in ln(consumption) from goods delivered
rows.explainer: Zero here (no goods); the cash branch has its own.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, other health care
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.6 (0.3-0.9): the share of excess deaths averted rests on trials of community packages delivered fully (Lassi & Bhutta 2015), not on a measure of the IRC's own care.

rows.label: Counterfactual, other health care
rows.explainer: Judgment 70% (50-90%): the IRC supports government facilities and runs mobile clinics where they have failed; without it some of those covered would reach other NGOs' or the ministry's care.

rows.label: The IRC's share of all resources behind the care
rows.explainer: Judgment 70% (50-90%): medicines and supplies from WHO, UNICEF and pooled funds, and ministry staff in the facilities the IRC supports, are not in its cost (Convention 2); partners the IRC sub-grants are (their cost is its own).

rows.label: Attribution share, other health care
rows.explainer: The shared attribution above.

rows.label: Share of reported reach that gets the service as studied
rows.explainer: Judgment 85% (70-95%), every branch: stock-outs, insecurity that closes facilities and programmes cut short by the 2025 US funding cuts (the IRC's USAID-funded work stopped in part during the year).

rows.label: Funging and leverage
rows.explainer: Judgment 1 (0.85-1.1), every branch: restricted grants (two thirds of revenue) fix most programme spending; a donor's unrestricted dollar may be replaced by a grant (<1) or pull in matched funding (>1).

rows.label: Missing-data discount, other health care
rows.explainer: Thin: no count of people covered (reach is spending over a judged cost) and no measured effect of the IRC's care. Counted less by the shared slider (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: All adjustments, other health care
rows.formula: hlt_evidence_adj * hlt_counterfactual_adj * attribution_share * implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * hlt_missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The branch's adjustments multiplied.

rows.label: Share of health spending on contraception
rows.explainer: Judgment 5% (2-10%): contraception is one of the four interventions the IRC says it will scale first (2025 Annual Report, Executive Summary p. 8: nutrition, immunization, contraception and cash), delivered inside its reproductive health care; no spending or count of users is published.

rows.label: Family planning spending (US$)
rows.explainer: Health spending × the contraception share.

rows.label: Family planning: the IRC's cost per couple-year of protection (US$)
rows.explainer: Judgment $45 ($15-100): the IRC's own cost-efficiency analysis of four family planning programmes found an average of $47 a couple-year of protection (rescue.org, 'Cost efficiency analysis: distributing family planning materials'); its SheCares pilot in Uganda's refugee settlements reached $14 and the WISH2ACTION programme in South Sudan $43-100.

rows.label: Family planning: couple-years of protection provided
rows.explainer: Spending ÷ the cost per couple-year.

rows.label: Family planning: value of a couple-year of protection (units of value)
rows.explainer: GiveWell's shared value of a year of modern contraception in low-income countries (deaths averted, income and wellbeing of unintended births avoided). Its deaths part (maternal and infant deaths of pregnancies averted) is a different channel from the excess crisis deaths other health care averts, so neither is counted twice.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, family planning
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.8 (0.6-1): the value per couple-year is GiveWell's modelled figure for stable settings; in crises, pregnancies averted per couple-year may be fewer (spacing already wider after displacement) or more (unmet need higher).

rows.label: Counterfactual, family planning
rows.explainer: Judgment 60% (40-85%): some users would switch from other providers or methods; in camps and conflict areas few others offer long-acting methods.

rows.label: The IRC's share of all resources behind the contraception
rows.explainer: Judgment 60% (40-80%): the contraceptives come mostly from UNFPA and the ministry staff deliver part of it.

rows.label: Missing-data discount, family planning
rows.explainer: Thin: no count of users or couple-years; reach is spending over a judged cost. Counted less by the shared slider.

rows.label: All adjustments, family planning
rows.formula: fp_evidence_adj * fp_counterfactual_adj * fp_attribution_share * implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * fp_missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The branch's adjustments multiplied.

rows.label: Children under five admitted to nutrition treatment, 2025

source.title: International Rescue Committee, 2025 Annual Report, Executive Summary

rows.explainer: Admissions counted by the IRC; most are treated as outpatients under the simplified (combined) protocol for severe and moderate wasting. The report doesn't say whether '2025' is the fiscal or the calendar year; every reach count here is taken as the fiscal year of the accounts (October 2024 to September 2025).

rows.label: Pregnant or lactating women admitted to nutrition programmes, 2025

source.title: International Rescue Committee, 2025 Annual Report, Executive Summary

rows.explainer: Admissions counted by the IRC.

rows.label: Nutrition: the IRC's cost per admission, without supplies others donate (US$)
rows.explainer: Judgment $110 (60-200): GiveWell's 'Malnutrition treatment CEA (IRC standard protocol), 2023' costs a child with severe wasting at about $55 to the IRC in Burkina Faso, before ready-to-use food from UNICEF; with supplies a treated child costs about $150-200, and insecure settings (Sudan, Gaza, Somalia) cost more than Burkina Faso.

rows.label: Nutrition spending (US$)
rows.explainer: Admissions × the cost per admission.

rows.label: Nutrition: share of children admitted with severe wasting
rows.explainer: Judgment 50% (30-70%): severely wasted children are about 30% of all wasted children worldwide (UNICEF/WHO/World Bank joint malnutrition estimates, 2023: 13.7 of 45 million), but a larger share of admissions, since screening finds them first and moderate cases are often referred to WFP's supplementary feeding instead; the IRC publishes no split of its 638,187 admissions.

rows.label: Nutrition: deaths per episode of severe wasting without treatment
rows.explainer: Judgment 10% (4-20%): in pooled cohorts children with severe wasting die about 11 times as often as others (Olofin et al. 2013, PLoS ONE, ten prospective studies); at a crisis under-five death rate of 1.5-2% a year, over an untreated episode of several months, that is roughly 5-15%. GiveWell's shared figure for Chad, a mortality ratio of 7 for untreated severe wasting (@givewell_chad.mortality_ratio_for_children_6_59_months_with_untreated_sam), is a check on the same order.

rows.label: Nutrition: share of those deaths treatment averts
rows.explainer: The shared figure for treating severe acute malnutrition (@relief_development.sam_treatment_deaths_averted_share, 60%, 40-80%): treated children die at about 3-5% in community programmes, against the 10% untreated above.

rows.label: Nutrition: deaths averted for a moderately wasted child, relative to a severely wasted one
rows.explainer: Judgment 20% (10-35%): GiveWell's IRC sheets put untreated-vs-treated mortality ratios at about 1.7 for moderate wasting against 3.3 for severe (its 2023 IRC standard-protocol sheet), on a baseline risk several times lower.

rows.label: Nutrition: value of a pregnant or lactating woman's admission, relative to a severely wasted child's
rows.explainer: Judgment 20% (0-50%): supplements for undernourished mothers raise birth weight and cut small-for-gestational-age births (Cochrane: balanced energy-protein supplementation, stillbirths RR about 0.6), a smaller and less certain effect on deaths than treating a wasted child.

rows.label: Nutrition: deaths averted per child admitted
rows.explainer: Untreated case fatality × the share averted, for the mix of severe and moderate cases.

rows.label: Nutrition: illness and development averted, as a share of the deaths' value
rows.explainer: Judgment 15% (0-40%): recovered children avoid the stunting and infections that follow wasting, beside the deaths averted.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, nutrition
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.6 (0.3-0.9): no trial compares treatment with none (it would be unethical); the effect rests on cohorts (Olofin et al. 2013).

rows.label: Counterfactual, nutrition
rows.explainer: Judgment 65% (45-85%): GiveWell's IRC sheet finds 13-40% of severe cases treated without the IRC in its Burkina Faso districts; in Sudan, Somalia and Gaza in 2025 others' treatment fell with the funding cuts.

rows.label: The IRC's share of all resources behind nutrition treatment
rows.explainer: Judgment 55% (40-80%): ready-to-use therapeutic food, about $40-60 a child, mostly comes from UNICEF and WFP and isn't in the IRC's cost; ministry health workers deliver part of the care.

rows.label: Missing-data discount, nutrition
rows.explainer: Thin: admissions are counted, but the effect of treatment is judged from cohorts with no trial against no treatment (templates.md glossary). Counted less by the shared slider.

rows.label: All adjustments, nutrition
rows.formula: nut_evidence_adj * nut_counterfactual_adj * nut_attribution_share * implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * nut_missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The branch's adjustments multiplied.

rows.label: Vaccine doses delivered by the IRC-led consortium in hard-to-reach conflict zones, 2022 to May 2026

source.title: International Rescue Committee, 2025 Annual Report
source.quote: As of May 2026, we had delivered more than 30 million vaccine doses in hard-to-reach conflict zones

rows.explainer: The IRC-led REACH consortium (Gavi-funded) in six countries; a cumulative count, so the year's doses are a judgment below.

rows.label: Share of the consortium's doses from 2022 to May 2026 delivered in the year to September 2025
rows.explainer: Judgment 27% (17-37%): the 30 million doses over the 4.4 years from January 2022 to May 2026 average 23% a year; more in later years as the consortium scaled and the cost per dose fell from $3.70 to $1.

rows.label: Vaccine doses delivered in the year to September 2025
rows.explainer: The cumulative doses × the year's share: about 8 million.

rows.label: Delivery cost per vaccine dose, 2025 (US$)

source.title: International Rescue Committee, 2025 Annual Report
source.quote: average delivery costs down from around $3.70 per dose in 2023 to around $1 in 2025

rows.explainer: The IRC's delivery cost per dose (staff, outreach, cold chain), not the vaccine, which Gavi and UNICEF supply; 'around $1' read as $0.8-1.3.

rows.label: Vaccination spending (US$)
rows.explainer: Doses × delivery cost per dose.

rows.label: Vaccination: doses per child reached
rows.explainer: Judgment 10 (7-14): a full routine schedule is 15-20 doses (BCG, polio, pentavalent, pneumococcal, rotavirus, measles); children found at outreach sites get part of it, some catch-up only.

rows.label: Vaccination: children reached
rows.explainer: Doses ÷ doses per child.

rows.label: Vaccination: deaths averted per zero- or under-dose child vaccinated
rows.explainer: Judgment 1% (0.4-2.5%): under-five mortality in the consortium's countries is about 8-11%; modelling of vaccines against ten pathogens in 98 low- and middle-income countries puts their effect at a large part of child deaths (Li et al. 2021, Lancet 397:398-408); a child given part of the schedule late, where measles and pneumonia kill most, gets a smaller share of that.

rows.label: Vaccination: illness averted, as a share of the deaths' value
rows.explainer: GiveWell's shared figure for illness averted by childhood vaccines (6%).

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, vaccination
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.75 (0.5-0.95): the vaccines' efficacy is from trials; the deaths per child is modelled, not measured, and cold chains in conflict zones lose potency.

rows.label: Counterfactual, vaccination
rows.explainer: Judgment 50% (30-80%): the children are zero-dose in areas the health system doesn't reach, but campaigns (polio, measles) and later routine contact reach part of them anyway.

rows.label: The IRC's share of all resources behind the doses
rows.explainer: Judgment 25% (15-45%): Gavi and UNICEF pay for the vaccines and cold chain (about $20-40 for a child's schedule) against the IRC's delivery at about $10 a child; ministry staff vaccinate at many sites.

rows.label: Missing-data discount, vaccination
rows.explainer: Thin: the year's doses are judged from a cumulative count, and deaths averted per child are modelled. Counted less by the shared slider.

rows.label: All adjustments, vaccination
rows.formula: vax_evidence_adj * vax_counterfactual_adj * vax_attribution_share * implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * vax_missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The branch's adjustments multiplied.

rows.label: People supported with improved water-supply services, 2025

source.title: International Rescue Committee, 2025 Annual Report, Executive Summary
source.quote: 2,513,058 people supported with improved water-supply services

rows.explainer: Counted by the IRC: water trucking, borehole repair and new supply in camps and host communities.

rows.label: Water: cost per person supplied for a year (US$)
rows.explainer: Judgment $15 (8-35): rehabilitating and running water points costs a few dollars a person a year; trucking in acute emergencies and new systems far more.

rows.label: Water spending (US$)
rows.explainer: People × cost per person.

rows.label: Water: share of the people supplied who are under five
rows.explainer: Judgment 16% (13-19%): the under-five share of populations in sub-Saharan Africa's crisis countries (UN WPP: about 15-18%).

rows.label: Water: yearly death rate of children under five in the areas supplied
rows.explainer: Judgment 2% a year (1.2-3%): under-five mortality of 6-14% over five years in the IRC's countries.

rows.label: Water: share of child deaths averted by a year of improved supply
rows.explainer: Judgment 4% (1-10%): the meta-analysis of water-treatment trials finds about a quarter fewer child deaths (Kremer et al. 2023, odds ratio about 0.7); more water from a better source without treatment does less, and part of the supply is short-lived trucking.

rows.label: Water: deaths averted per person supplied
rows.explainer: Children's share × their death rate × the share averted.

rows.label: Water: illness averted, as a share of the deaths' value
rows.explainer: Judgment 10% (0-30%): diarrhoeal illness and cholera outbreaks averted; the time saved fetching water is in unmodelled_benefits_adj.

rows.label: Water: value of water-fetching time saved, as a share of consumption
rows.explainer: The shared figure for time saved fetching water, mostly women's and girls' (@water.time_saved_consumption_share, 0.75% of consumption, 0-3%).

rows.label: Water: gain in ln(consumption) from time saved, per person
rows.explainer: A side effect of the water supply: time freed for work, school or care, valued at consumption. Read at the shared side-effect weight.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, water
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.5 (0.3-0.8): the effect is from household water-treatment trials, not supply in emergencies.

rows.label: Counterfactual, water
rows.explainer: Judgment 70% (50-90%): other agencies and the camps' water committees would supply part of it.

rows.label: The IRC's share of all resources behind the water supply
rows.explainer: Judgment 80% (60-100%): communities' labour and local authorities' systems.

rows.label: Missing-data discount, water
rows.explainer: Thin: people are counted, but the effect is from other delivery (household treatment trials). Counted less by the shared slider.

rows.label: All adjustments, water
rows.formula: wash_evidence_adj * wash_counterfactual_adj * wash_attribution_share * implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * wash_missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The branch's adjustments multiplied.

rows.label: Cash and vouchers given, 2025 (US$)

source.title: International Rescue Committee, 2025 Annual Report, Executive Summary

rows.explainer: Counted by the IRC: emergency and anticipatory cash and vouchers in crisis countries.

rows.label: People reached with cash or vouchers, 2025

source.title: International Rescue Committee, 2025 Annual Report, Executive Summary
source.quote: 1,546,345 people reached with cash assistance or vouchers

rows.explainer: Counted by the IRC.

rows.label: Cash: cost of delivering a dollar of cash (targeting, staff, transfer fees), per dollar given
rows.explainer: Judgment 25 cents (12-45): the IRC's cost-efficiency analyses of humanitarian cash find costs falling to under 20 cents a dollar in large programmes and above 40 in small or insecure ones.

rows.label: Cash spending (US$)
rows.explainer: Cash given plus its delivery.

rows.label: Cash: value per person reached (US$)
rows.explainer: About {{row:cash_per_person}} a person.

rows.label: Cash: 2025 US dollars in 2017 prices
rows.explainer: US consumer prices 2017 ÷ 2025, so 2025 dollars are set against consumption in 2017 international dollars.

rows.label: Cash: time the cash covers needs (years)
rows.explainer: Judgment 3 months (1-6): the IRC's emergency cash is mostly one to three monthly payments, its anticipatory cash up to five months (the Somalia drought response in the 2025 Annual Report).

rows.label: Cash: gain in ln(consumption) per person
rows.formula: cash_years_covered * ln(1 + cash_per_person * cash_price_level * ppp_factor / (baseline_consumption * cash_years_covered))
rows.explainer: The site's rule for a transfer used within a year: the months covered × ln(1 + the cash at local prices ÷ the consumption of those months).

rows.label: Cash: effects on others through local markets, as a share of the recipients' gain
rows.explainer: A side effect: cash spent locally raises traders' and neighbours' incomes (Egger et al. 2022, Econometrica: a local multiplier of about 2.5 in rural Kenya) and can raise prices where markets are thin (-). Judgment +5% (-5% to +25%): emergency cash is small and in disrupted markets.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, cash
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.95 (0.85-1): the money is the benefit; the count of people may include some registered twice across rounds or programmes. Diversion and fraud are in se_diversion_share, transfer fees in the delivery cost.

rows.label: Counterfactual, cash
rows.explainer: Judgment 85% (60-100%): other agencies (WFP, NGOs) might have reached some of the same people.

rows.label: The IRC's share of all resources behind the cash
rows.explainer: Judgment 95% (85-100%): the cash and its delivery are the IRC's own spending; partners and mobile-money networks add a little.

rows.label: Missing-data adjustment, cash (measured)
rows.explainer: Measured: the dollars and the people are counted, and the transfer is itself the benefit; no discount.

rows.label: All adjustments, cash
rows.formula: cash_evidence_adj * cash_counterfactual_adj * cash_attribution_share * implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * cash_missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The branch's adjustments multiplied.

rows.label: Livelihoods spending: the rest of economic well-being (US$)
rows.explainer: Economic well-being less cash: agriculture, savings groups, small-business grants and vocational training; never below zero.

rows.label: Livelihoods: cost per household reached (US$)
rows.explainer: The shared figure for livelihood programmes abroad (@relief_development.livelihood_cost_per_household, $200, $80-500): savings groups cost tens of dollars a household, business grants and training several hundred.

rows.label: Livelihoods: households reached
rows.explainer: Spending ÷ cost per household.

rows.label: Livelihoods: household size
rows.explainer: The shared household sizes of four of the IRC's large programme countries.

rows.label: Livelihoods: consumption gain per household reached, share of consumption
rows.explainer: The shared figure for livelihood programmes abroad (@relief_development.livelihood_package_consumption_gain, 3%, 0.5-8%): savings-promotion trials in sub-Saharan Africa find a small gain (Steinert et al. 2018); graduation programmes, which cost far more, about 5-10% (Banerjee et al. 2015).

rows.label: Livelihoods: years the gain lasts
rows.explainer: The shared figure for livelihood programmes abroad (@relief_development.livelihood_gain_years, 2 years, 1-4): gains fade; assets and skills keep part.

rows.label: Livelihoods: gain in ln(consumption) per person, discounted
rows.explainer: The gain for each year it lasts, discounted.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, livelihoods
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.75 (0.4-1): trials of similar programmes (Steinert et al. 2018), in less disrupted places.

rows.label: Counterfactual, livelihoods
rows.explainer: Judgment 90% (70-100%): few others offer these programmes in the same camps and districts.

rows.label: The IRC's share of all resources behind livelihoods
rows.explainer: Judgment 80% (60-100%): participants' own savings and time, and microfinance partners.

rows.label: Missing-data discount, livelihoods
rows.explainer: Thin: reach is spending over a judged cost and the effect is from other programmes' trials.

rows.label: All adjustments, livelihoods
rows.formula: liv_evidence_adj * liv_counterfactual_adj * liv_attribution_share * implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * liv_missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The branch's adjustments multiplied.

rows.label: Visits to safe spaces by women and girls, 2025

source.title: International Rescue Committee, 2025 Annual Report, Executive Summary
source.quote: 1,290,040 visits to safe spaces by women and girls

rows.explainer: Counted by the IRC: women's and girls' safe spaces, where gender-based violence case management and psychosocial support are given.

rows.label: Children supported through IRC safe spaces, 2025

source.title: International Rescue Committee, 2025 Annual Report, Executive Summary
source.quote: 72,663 children supported through IRC safe spaces

rows.explainer: Counted by the IRC.

rows.label: Protection: visits per woman or girl
rows.explainer: Judgment 5 (3-10): case management and group sessions run over several weeks; some come once for information or a dignity kit.

rows.label: Protection: women, girls and children counted in safe spaces
rows.explainer: Unique women and girls (visits ÷ visits each) plus children.

rows.label: Protection: cost per person reached by all safety work (US$)
rows.explainer: Judgment $150 ($60-400): gender-based violence case management, child protection case work, legal aid and community protection; a case handled over months costs hundreds of dollars, group sessions and information far less.

rows.label: Protection: people reached by the safety work
rows.explainer: The safety spending ÷ the cost per person, at least the counted safe-space reach: the counts cover only safe spaces, not the child protection, legal and case work the rest of the line pays for.

rows.label: Protection: share of those reached with a mental disorder
rows.explainer: The shared WHO prevalence of depression, anxiety, post-traumatic stress, bipolar disorder and schizophrenia in conflict-affected populations (@humanitarian_response.conflict_mental_disorder_prevalence, 22.1%, 18.8-25.7%).

rows.label: Protection: improvement in mental health for those with a disorder (SD)
rows.explainer: The shared figure for broad protection work (@humanitarian_response.protection_mental_health_effect_sd, 0.2 SD, 0.05-0.4): focused psychosocial interventions in humanitarian settings show small to moderate falls in distress (Purgato et al. 2018); the IRC's protection is mostly community protection, safe spaces and referral, with case management for survivors of violence for fewer. Those without a disorder count at nothing here; their gain and violence prevented are in unmodelled_benefits_adj.

rows.label: Protection: years the improvement lasts
rows.explainer: Judgment a year (6 months to 2 years), fading linearly: trials measure a few months after the sessions.

rows.label: Protection: discount over the years the effect lasts
rows.explainer: The shared discount rate at the effect's midpoint, as the wellbeing template discounts a fading effect.

rows.label: Protection: WELLBYs per person reached
rows.explainer: Share with a disorder × the effect in SD × its years × a half (linear fade) × the discount × the shared WELLBYs per SD-year.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, protection
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.6 (0.3-0.9): small trials, mixed results (Purgato et al. 2018).

rows.label: Counterfactual, protection
rows.explainer: Judgment 90% (70-100%): few other services for survivors of violence in these places.

rows.label: The IRC's share of all resources behind protection
rows.explainer: Judgment 80% (60-100%): community volunteers and local women's organisations the IRC works with.

rows.label: Missing-data discount, protection
rows.explainer: Thin: visits counted, the effect judged from other programmes' trials.

rows.label: All adjustments, protection
rows.formula: pro_evidence_adj * pro_counterfactual_adj * pro_attribution_share * implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * pro_missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The branch's adjustments multiplied.

rows.label: Children and youth supported in learning programmes, 2025

source.title: International Rescue Committee, 2025 Annual Report, Executive Summary
source.quote: 602,546 children and youth supported in learning programs

rows.explainer: Counted by the IRC.

rows.label: Education: learning gain per child (standard deviations)
rows.explainer: The median effect on learning of randomised evaluations of education programmes in low- and middle-income countries (@education.learning_gain_sd_median_rct_lmic, Evans & Yuan 2022, 0.10 SD, 0.03-0.2); the IRC's PlayMatters reports above-average gains in Ethiopia at $38 a child, without a published effect size.

rows.label: Education: adult earnings gain per SD of skill still there in adult life
rows.explainer: The site's one figure for low- and middle-income countries (@education.earnings_gain_per_sd_adult_skills_lmic: 20%, 10% to 30%), from the Center for Global Development's review of the studies linking adults' reading and maths to their earnings, per SD of skill still there in adult life.

rows.label: Education: share of the learning gain still there in adult life
rows.explainer: The site's one figure (@education.test_gain_persistence_to_adulthood: 40%, 20% to 70%): test-score gains fade, a fifth to a half of a year's learning carrying into the next grade in Pakistan's schools (Andrabi and others 2011).

rows.label: Education: years from the programme to adult earnings
rows.explainer: The shared figure for primary-age education abroad (@education.years_primary_programme_to_work, 10 years, 6-15): children of primary age start work in 5-15 years.

rows.label: Years the earnings gain lasts
rows.explainer: GiveWell's shared years of long-term income gains.

rows.label: Household sharing of income gains
rows.explainer: GiveWell's shared multiplier.

rows.label: Education: gain in ln(consumption) per child, discounted to today
rows.formula: ln(1 + edu_learning_gain_sd * edu_earnings_per_sd * edu_persistence) * pv_annuity_due(1, $discount_rate, working_years) * (1 + $discount_rate) ^ (0 - edu_years_until_work) * resource_sharing_multiplier
rows.explainer: ln(1 + learning gain × earnings per SD × persistence) for each working year, discounted, after the wait to adult work, shared with the household.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, education
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.6 (0.3-1): Evans & Yuan find the median effect of small trials several times that of large ones, and most trials are outside crises, where schooling is disrupted.

rows.label: Counterfactual, education
rows.explainer: Judgment 85% (60-100%): displaced children mostly have no other school.

rows.label: The IRC's share of all resources behind education
rows.explainer: Judgment 80% (60-100%): ministry teachers and community volunteers in part of the learning centres.

rows.label: Missing-data discount, education
rows.explainer: Thin: children counted, the effect from other programmes' trials.

rows.label: All adjustments, education
rows.formula: edu_evidence_adj * edu_counterfactual_adj * edu_attribution_share * implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * edu_missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The branch's adjustments multiplied.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment: outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only
rows.formula: (hlt_dalys_unadjusted * hlt_evidence_adj + fp_dalys_unadjusted * fp_evidence_adj + nut_dalys_unadjusted * nut_evidence_adj + vax_dalys_unadjusted * vax_evidence_adj + wash_dalys_unadjusted * wash_evidence_adj + cash_dalys_unadjusted * cash_evidence_adj + liv_dalys_unadjusted * liv_evidence_adj + pro_dalys_unadjusted * pro_evidence_adj + edu_dalys_unadjusted * edu_evidence_adj) / (hlt_dalys_unadjusted + fp_dalys_unadjusted + nut_dalys_unadjusted + vax_dalys_unadjusted + wash_dalys_unadjusted + cash_dalys_unadjusted + liv_dalys_unadjusted + pro_dalys_unadjusted + edu_dalys_unadjusted)
rows.explainer: Outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only: each branch applies its own row, weighted by its outcome before adjustments in healthy years (each through its unit's fixed bridge).

rows.label: Counterfactual: outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only
rows.formula: (hlt_dalys_unadjusted * hlt_counterfactual_adj + fp_dalys_unadjusted * fp_counterfactual_adj + nut_dalys_unadjusted * nut_counterfactual_adj + vax_dalys_unadjusted * vax_counterfactual_adj + wash_dalys_unadjusted * wash_counterfactual_adj + cash_dalys_unadjusted * cash_counterfactual_adj + liv_dalys_unadjusted * liv_counterfactual_adj + pro_dalys_unadjusted * pro_counterfactual_adj + edu_dalys_unadjusted * edu_counterfactual_adj) / (hlt_dalys_unadjusted + fp_dalys_unadjusted + nut_dalys_unadjusted + vax_dalys_unadjusted + wash_dalys_unadjusted + cash_dalys_unadjusted + liv_dalys_unadjusted + pro_dalys_unadjusted + edu_dalys_unadjusted)
rows.explainer: Outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only: each branch applies its own row, weighted by its outcome before adjustments in healthy years (each through its unit's fixed bridge).

rows.label: Missing-data discount: outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only
rows.formula: (hlt_dalys_unadjusted * hlt_missing_data_adj + fp_dalys_unadjusted * fp_missing_data_adj + nut_dalys_unadjusted * nut_missing_data_adj + vax_dalys_unadjusted * vax_missing_data_adj + wash_dalys_unadjusted * wash_missing_data_adj + cash_dalys_unadjusted * cash_missing_data_adj + liv_dalys_unadjusted * liv_missing_data_adj + pro_dalys_unadjusted * pro_missing_data_adj + edu_dalys_unadjusted * edu_missing_data_adj) / (hlt_dalys_unadjusted + fp_dalys_unadjusted + nut_dalys_unadjusted + vax_dalys_unadjusted + wash_dalys_unadjusted + cash_dalys_unadjusted + liv_dalys_unadjusted + pro_dalys_unadjusted + edu_dalys_unadjusted)
rows.explainer: Outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only: each branch applies its own row, weighted by its outcome before adjustments in healthy years (each through its unit's fixed bridge).

rows.label: All adjustments combined: outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only
rows.formula: (hlt_dalys + fp_dalys + nut_dalys + vax_dalys + wash_dalys + cash_dalys + liv_dalys + pro_dalys + edu_dalys) / (hlt_dalys_unadjusted + fp_dalys_unadjusted + nut_dalys_unadjusted + vax_dalys_unadjusted + wash_dalys_unadjusted + cash_dalys_unadjusted + liv_dalys_unadjusted + pro_dalys_unadjusted + edu_dalys_unadjusted)
rows.explainer: Outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only: each branch applies its own row, weighted by its outcome before adjustments in healthy years (each through its unit's fixed bridge).

rows.label: Side effect: violence prevented by protection and safe spaces, as a share of the result
rows.explainer: Protection is valued only through mental health; violence it prevents (community programmes in IRC trials have mixed effects on intimate-partner violence) is a small further gain. +0.5% (0 to +2%), against protection's small share of the result.

rows.label: Side effect: the IRC's research (Airbel Impact Lab, cost analyses) used by others, as a share of the result
rows.explainer: The IRC says it produces a fifth of humanitarian impact evidence (2025 Annual Report p. 10); other agencies adopting cheaper protocols (the simplified malnutrition protocol, cash) gain from it. +1% (0 to +4%).

rows.label: Side effect: aid diverted or lost in conflict zones, as a share of the result
rows.explainer: Aid taken by armed groups, fraud and losses in transit; humanitarian agencies' reported losses run around 1-3% of spending, more in the hardest places (Sudan, Somalia, Gaza). -2% (-5% to 0).

rows.label: Side effect: harm from safeguarding failures, as a share of the result
rows.explainer: Sexual exploitation and abuse by aid workers and contractors, reported across the sector each year. -0.5% (-2% to 0).

rows.label: Side effects not in the branches, as a share of the modelled result
rows.explainer: The signed side effects above, each estimated against the result; contraception is its own branch, time saved fetching water is in the water branch and market effects in the cash branch, and programmes cut short by the 2025 funding cuts are in implementation_adj, so none is counted here again.

rows.label: Other health care: units of value (deaths, after adjustments)
rows.explainer: People covered × deaths averted × value, after the branch's adjustments.

rows.label: Family planning: units of value, after adjustments
rows.explainer: Couple-years × the shared value of one.

rows.label: Nutrition: units of value, after adjustments
rows.formula: (nut_children + nut_plw * nut_plw_relative_value / (nut_sam_share + (1 - nut_sam_share) * nut_mam_relative_risk)) * nut_deaths_per_child * value_per_death_under5 * (1 + nut_morbidity_value_ratio) * nut_total_adj
rows.explainer: Children admitted, plus mothers at their relative value to a severely wasted child (so ÷ the child mix), × deaths averted per child × a child's value, with illness.

rows.label: Vaccination: units of value, after adjustments
rows.explainer: Children × deaths averted × value, with illness.

rows.label: Water: units of value, after adjustments
rows.explainer: People × (deaths averted × value, with illness + time saved on the log-income scale, a side effect).

rows.label: Cash: units of value, after adjustments
rows.explainer: People × ln gain × the shared value of ln(consumption), with market effects (a side effect, read at the side-effect weight).

rows.label: Livelihoods: units of value, after adjustments
rows.explainer: People × ln gain × value.

rows.label: Education: units of value, after adjustments
rows.explainer: Children × ln gain × value.

rows.formula: hlt_uov + fp_uov + nut_uov + vax_uov + wash_uov + cash_uov + liv_uov + edu_uov
